parts.text: This question is about sulfuric acid, H 2 SO 4 .

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Dilute sulfuric acid and aqueous sodium hydroxide can be used to prepare sodium sulfate crystals using a method that involves titration. The apparatus for titration is shown in Fig. 4.1. Fig. 4.1 Thymolphthalein is used as an indicator for this titration.

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) 25.0 cm 3 of aqueous sodium hydroxide, NaOH, of concentration 0.100 mol / dm 3 is neutralised by 20.0 cm 3 of dilute sulfuric acid, H 2 SO 4 . The equation for the reaction is shown. 2NaOH + H 2 SO 4 → Na 2 SO 4 + 2H 2 O Calculate the concentration of H 2 SO 4 using the following steps. ● Calculate the number of moles of NaOH used. .............................. mol ● Determine the number of moles of H 2 SO 4 that react with the NaOH. .............................. mol ● Calculate the concentration of H 2 SO 4 . .............................. mol / dm 3 [3]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) In another experiment, 48.0 cm 3 of hydrogen gas, H 2 , is produced. The experiment is carried out at room temperature and pressure, r.t.p.
